A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TS-roots research. All 33 pages, including Appendices A-I, are available and readable; text, equations, algorithms and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendices D/I report original optimization experiments on benchmark functions and a ten-bar truss, including comparator and sensitivity results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, truss, inner-loop optimization, MES and sensitivity results reported in v2.

M1.justification: The sampling construction, rootfinding, starting-point selection and sample-average procedure are unchanged. The revised approximation language qualifies the existing construction; Algorithms 1-7 retain their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Schwefel, Rosenbrock, Levy, Ackley, Powell and Hartmann problems and ten-bar truss, with unchanged dimensions and test scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain TS-DSRF, TS-RF, EI and LCB; random multistart and genetic optimization; appendix grid/LHS initializations; and the same MES variants.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain the same initialization, preprocessing, iteration budgets, metrics, restart matching and stopping procedures. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The covariance-approximation comparison, Appendix D starting-set analysis and Appendix I initialization and sample-average sensitivity studies are unchanged. The new theoretical qualification adds no empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain medians and interquartile ranges from 20 runs for the main BO comparisons and ten runs for MES. Run counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2-7 and 9-13 retain the same plotted results, and their associated numerical statements, rankings and empirical findings are unchanged. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Eqs. (2) and (10) replace exact prior factorization with an approximation. Appendix C.1 retracts the exact-representation statement and specifies a third-order approximation whose moment functions differ at fourth and higher even orders. This substantially revises the mathematical status of the foundational sampling representation, although the remaining proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about rootfinding, dimensional scaling, BO/MES performance and the sample-average formulation.

C2.justification: Appendix C.1 newly acknowledges the separable approximation's higher-order moment mismatch and explains separability as a useful property of that representation. Other interpretations, limitations and future-work statements remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The sampling implementation, spectral truncation rules, hyperparameters, hardware/software descriptions and code-access statement are retained. The approximation qualification supplies no new implementation instructions.

R1.justification: Section 5 and all 53 references are unchanged. The added acknowledgments provide credits and funding information without changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording revisions in Section 3.1 and Appendix C.1, adds an appendix cross-reference and acknowledgments, and updates the arXiv stamp. The broader narrative and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: Acknowledgments occupy previously blank space on page 12. Expanded Appendix C.1 text moves part of the eigenfunction formula onto page 22 and shifts subsequent material. Figures and captions are retained without redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical accuracy and transparency by replacing the exact separability assertion with an explicit approximation and acknowledging its higher-order moment mismatch. The benefit is limited because the consequences for the unchanged posterior-sampling and sample-average arguments are not examined; the empirical evidence remains identical.
